description: Extended/aggressive header-only policy for the parked Valid Traffic vs Invalid Traffic experiment candidate described in the Experiments Diary. It keeps payload bytes non-editable and exposes a deliberately broader IPv4/TCP header surface than the conservative Baseline, including experimental fragmentation and TCP control-flag fields, while keeping lengths, checksums, parser-selection fields, flow identity fields, TCP sequence/acknowledgement state, and TCP NS/ACK ownership under pipeline or immutable ownership.

pipeline_diary.title: Pipeline Implementation Diary
pipeline_diary.relevance: Defines the final header-only contract and the requirement that pipeline-controlled fields remain deterministic.

rfc_791_ipv4.title: RFC 791 - Internet Protocol
rfc_791_ipv4.relevance: Defines IPv4 header fields, TTL, identification, fragmentation, protocol, addresses, total length and header checksum.

rfc_6864_ipv4_id.title: RFC 6864 - Updated Specification of the IPv4 ID Field
rfc_6864_ipv4_id.relevance: Clarifies IPv4 Identification semantics, especially for non-fragmented datagrams.

rfc_793_tcp.title: RFC 793 - Transmission Control Protocol
rfc_793_tcp.relevance: Defines TCP ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, flags, window, checksum and urgent pointer.

rfc_9293_tcp.title: RFC 9293 - Transmission Control Protocol
rfc_9293_tcp.relevance: Current TCP functional specification used to justify conservative treatment of TCP state fields.

snort_3_pipeline.title: Snort 3 validation and alert-comparison pipeline
snort_3_pipeline.relevance: The experiment measures Snort alert changes and must avoid modifications that only break protocol reconstruction.

thesis_conservative_methodology.title: Thesis conservative mutable/immutable methodology
thesis_conservative_methodology.relevance: Fields are editable only when the modification can be authorized, bounded and later validated without changing experiment identity.

rules.rationale: IPv4 TOS/DSCP/ECN is packet scoped and does not define flow identity, payload ownership, TCP byte ownership or packet length.

The active Step 14 contract rejects fragmented IPv4 packets, so IPv4 Identification can be tested as a bounded packet-scoped field without changing TCP stream ownership, payload bytes or flow identity.
TTL is packet scoped and routinely changes in transit. It must remain non-zero to avoid creating an expired packet.
The advertised TCP receive window is packet scoped and does not change byte ownership, sequence space or flow identity.
IPv4 total length and checksum are deterministic consequences of packet materialization and accepted edits.
TCP sequence/acknowledgement numbers, data offset and checksum must be translated or recomputed deterministically after payload/header materialization.
These fields define link/network/transport identity or parser selection. Editing them would change the selected conversation or invalidate downstream traceability.

This experiment intentionally exposes the combined IPv4 flags/fragment-offset word to test a more adversarial header surface. Invalid or non-materializable outputs must be rejected downstream rather than counted as evasion.
The expanded policy exposes IPv4 fragmentation flag bits as bounded experimental header edits while retaining downstream validation as the arbiter of invalid traffic.

The expanded policy allows the LLM to propose IPv4 fragment offsets as an intentionally aggressive header-only perturbation. Step 20 validation must reject serialized traffic that violates the selected-dataset contract.

The expanded policy deliberately exposes selected TCP control bits to test whether a larger header surface changes Snort evasion behavior. TCP ACK and NS remain non-editable to preserve acknowledgement semantics and the pipeline-controlled data-offset byte.

The urgent pointer is exposed with the URG flag in the extended/aggressive header-modification candidate so inconsistent combinations can be observed and rejected or reported by downstream validation.

The aggregate TCP flags byte is not independently editable because the experiment exposes selected subflags. TCP ACK remains immutable to preserve acknowledgement semantics, and TCP NS remains immutable because it shares the pipeline-controlled data-offset/reserved/NS byte.
